title: Article 119 — Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business

content.overview: Article 119 provides that Parliament may, for the purpose of the timely completion of financial business, regulate by law the procedure of, and the conduct of business in, each House of Parliament in relation to any financial matter or to any Bill for the appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India, and if any provision of any law so made is inconsistent with any rule made by a House under Article 118 or with any rule or standing order under Article 118(2) transitional, such provision shall prevail.
content.glance: Parliament may by law regulate procedure for timely completion of financial business; such law prevails over House rules under Art 118 if inconsistent.
content.study:
Article 119 allows Parliament to legislate special procedure for financial business to ensure timely completion. Statutory financial procedure overrides inconsistent House-made rules under Article 118.

Examination: purpose (timely completion); scope (financial matters / Appropriation Bills); supremacy over Art 118 rules.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law regulate procedure and conduct of business in each House relating to financial matters or Appropriation Bills for timely completion of financial business. Such law prevails over inconsistent Article 118 rules.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the effect of Article 119?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 119 empowers Parliament to regulate by law the procedure of and the conduct of business in each House in relation to any financial matter or any Bill for appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India, for the purpose of timely completion of financial business. If such a law is inconsistent with any rule made by a House under Article 118, the law prevails.

examTips: Financial procedure law can override House rules under Art 118.

keyTakeaways: Art 119: statutory financial procedure prevails over House rules.
